title: Reading and changing text/content safely
learningObjectives: Explain reading and changing text/content safely and update browser documents with safe DOM and event patterns.

understand.concept: DOM properties such as textContent and innerText read or update text, while innerHTML parses or replaces markup. textContent is usually the safer choice for inserting untrusted text because it does not interpret the value as HTML.
understand.whyItMatters: Unsafe HTML insertion can create cross-site scripting vulnerabilities. Keep data and markup separate, validate data, and use safe DOM APIs for learner or user-generated content.
understand.analogy: textContent writes words onto the page; innerHTML asks the browser to interpret a string as markup.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; actual DOM, event, and security behaviour follows browser platform rules.

explain.narrative: The string is displayed as text rather than parsed as an image element. This avoids executing markup from the supplied string.

examples.explanation: The string is displayed as text rather than parsed as an image element. This avoids executing markup from the supplied string.
examples.expectedOutput: The browser page updates in response to safe DOM operations or user events.

practise.guidedTask: Update a message using textContent. Compare the result with innerHTML using a harmless markup string, and explain the security difference.
practise.independentTask: Build a small interactive component using DOM methods and event listeners. Handle missing elements and user input safely.
hints: Keep event handlers focused and avoid duplicate listeners.
Use event delegation for suitable dynamic lists.

questions.prompt: Which property inserts a string as text without parsing it as HTML?
questions.explanation: textContent treats the assigned value as text rather than HTML markup.

questions.prompt: What is a safe DOM update pattern for user-provided text?
options: Set textContent on an existing element
Build an HTML string and assign it to innerHTML
questions.answer: Set textContent on an existing element
questions.explanation: textContent treats the value as text and avoids parsing untrusted markup.
